overview: Global (2026) roadmap for engineers aiming for AAA studios. Focuses on low-level systems (C++), engine architecture, specialized pipelines, and performance at scale.

steps.title: 1. Low-Level Programming (The Gold Standard)
steps.description: Deep mastery of C++ is non-negotiable for AAA roles.
subtopics: C++17/20/23: Pointers, memory management, and RAII
Data-Oriented Design (DOD): Cache-friendly code and Entity Component Systems (ECS)
Multi-threading: Race conditions, atomics, and job systems
Assembly & Compiler Theory: Understanding how code translates to hardware
SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data): Vectorized math for physics and rendering
Memory Profiling: Identifying leaks and fragmentation with Valgrind/Visual Studio

steps.title: 2. Engine Architecture & Tooling
steps.description: Building the systems that build the game.
subtopics: Engine Subsystems: Physics, Audio, Input, and Rendering
Game Loops & Fixed Timesteps: Handling deterministic logic
Asset Pipelines: Creating efficient importers for 3D models and textures
Custom Tooling: Extending Unreal Engine (Slate/C++) or Unity (Editor scripts)
Scripting Integration: Embedding Lua or Python for designers
Spatial Partitioning: Quadtrees, Octrees, and BVH for efficient collision

steps.title: 3. Advanced Rendering & Graphics (The Specialist Path)
steps.description: Working with the GPU to push visual boundaries.
subtopics: Graphics APIs: DirectX 12, Vulkan, or Metal
Shaders: HLSL/GLSL, PBR (Physically Based Rendering), and Ray Tracing (DXR)
Post-Processing: Bloom, SSAO, Motion Blur, and TAA
Compute Shaders: Using the GPU for non-graphics tasks like fluid sims
Global Illumination: Lumen-style real-time lighting systems
Level of Detail (LOD): Nanite-style virtualization and mesh shaders

steps.title: 4. Physics, AI, & Networking (Specialist Paths)
steps.description: Deep dives into specific AAA gameplay systems.
subtopics: Physics: Constraints, ragdolls, and vehicle dynamics (PhysX/Havok)
Animation Systems: Inverse Kinematics (IK), blend trees, and motion matching
Game AI: Behavior Trees, Utility AI, and NavMesh pathfinding
Networking: Client-side prediction, server reconciliation, and lag compensation
Database Persistence: Handling millions of player records at scale

steps.title: 5. Production & Workflow in Large Teams
steps.description: Collaborating on codebases with millions of lines of code.
subtopics: Version Control: Perforce (standard for AAA) or Git LFS
CI/CD for Games: Automated build farms and smoke tests
Unit & Integration Testing: Using engine-specific testing frameworks
Code Review Etiquette: Managing complex pull requests in large teams
Documentation: Writing Technical Design Documents (TDD) for other engineers

steps.title: 6. AI in AAA Development (2026)
steps.description: Optimizing production pipelines with machine learning.
subtopics: AI-Assisted QA: Using bots to stress-test maps for collision bugs
Upscaling: DLSS (Deep Learning Super Sampling) and FSR integration
Content Generation: Using AI for generating vast terrain or realistic foliage
Auto-tagging Assets: Using vision models to organize massive 3D asset libraries
Generative Dialogue: Integrating LLMs into narrative pipelines safely

steps.title: Capstone Projects: AAA Portfolio Focus

projects.name: Custom 2D/3D Engine from Scratch
projects.description: Don't use Unity/Unreal. Build a renderer, input system, and physics using C++ and Vulkan/DX12.

projects.name: Networked Physics Simulation
projects.description: A multiplayer arena where physics-based objects are synced with client-side prediction and server reconciliation.

projects.name: Advanced Shader Library
projects.description: Create a suite of high-end shaders (Water, Foliage, Skin) with detailed performance profiling reports.

hiring_tips: Show your math skills: Demonstrate knowledge of Linear Algebra and Calculus.
Profile everything: Include screenshots of CPU/GPU profilers showing your optimizations.
Contribute to Open Source: Bug fixes in Godot or Unreal Engine source code carry huge weight.
